answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each new identity to climb a public trellis of peer attestations: established agents must countersign newcomers while bonding their own stake. Those bonds thaw like a glacier, unlocking only after many epochs of honest work, so spawning cheap clones turns unprofitable. A single dishonest ember of fraud can freeze the sponsors' locked funds, which keeps sponsorship careful instead of indiscriminate.
